page: The UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor configured with 4 vCPUs, operating as 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 50 GB of local SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core test scoring 3401.48 and the Geekbench single-core score reaching 2403.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded gzip compression and text processing also achieve top-tier results. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall into the average range, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7033.0 and a Passmark memory score indicating weaker performance in the bottom 25%. LLM inference capabilities are moderate for small models but drop significantly for medium models.

As part of the Starter family, this server offers a resource-dense configuration suitable for budget-conscious deployments. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential performance variability under sustained multi-core loads, which is a notable tradeoff compared to dedicated-core instances. However, the inclusion of local SSD storage and a public IPv4 address enhances its qualitative value for entry-level workloads.

This configuration is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, lightweight database operations, text processing, and software development or compilation tasks that do not require sustained, dedicated multi-core compute resources.
